title: Account-isolated golden-set evaluator with local-first telemetry and DP summaries
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an account-scoped eval runner that executes a small, customer-provided golden set inside the customer's dedicated/private deployment. The runner must produce regression signals tied to model or config changes while ensuring no raw customer artifacts leave the customer boundary. Goals: (a) enable per-account quality gates for canary/rollout decisions; (b) provide compact, privacy-preserving summaries suitable for Redwood Console and alerting; (c) support on-prem/VPC and dedicated modes with minimal host-side dependencies. Constraints: non-negotiable requirement that golden-set contents are never stored in Redwood-managed storage; telemetry must be differentially private or encrypted and aggregated; runner must integrate with existing rollout automation (canary thresholds, automatic rollback).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Eval runner can be deployed as an ephemeral container inside a customer's Dedicated or Private environment and execute a configurable golden set (size 10-200 examples) on model+config change triggers. 2) Raw golden-set payloads and per-example outputs remain in customer storage (S3/GCS/Vault) only; Redwood receives only an encrypted aggregate blob or DP-protected metrics. 3) Console shows per-account regression score and a pass/fail gate used by rollout automation. 4) Integration tests (ENG-4120) validate that a simulated regression delta > 4% blocks a canary rollout. 5) Security review completed and KMS/HSM integration verified in Private mode.

2025-02-18 - Priya Kapoor (Security): Recommended threat model additions: encrypted-at-rest golden set in customer S3, signed results, and tenant-scoped KMS keys. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-02-22 - Engineering (ENG-4120): PoC runs inside a Dedicated cluster using ephemeral Kubernetes Job; output is a serialized metrics blob encrypted with customer KMS and posted to Redwood ingest endpoint. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1892

2025-02-26 - Product review (Maya + Liam): Trade-off: stricter DP (epsilon <= 1) reduces signal; teams voted to start with configurable DP summaries (epsilon=2 default) and allow stricter settings per-customer SLA. Documented in design doc.
